transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess what finally made me come in is that it’s gotten noticeable to other people, not just something in my head. Like, sometimes I feel like I’m moving through water — everything takes me forever. I’ll sit there before answering someone, even a simple question, like my brain and body are lagging. Getting up out of a chair can feel like this whole process.

And then other times it’s the opposite. I’ll be in my apartment just pacing back and forth, rubbing my hands together, like I’m trying to get rid of the feeling after a bad customer service call or something. It’s not subtle anymore. People can see it, and that’s… kind of embarrassing, honestly. So I figured I should come talk to someone.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, maybe not every single minute of every day, but most of the time since this started, it’s been there. Like this heavy background feeling — sadness, guilt, not really being interested in things the way I used to, and then the sleep being messed up too.

Some weeks are a little lighter, where I can kind of function and tell myself maybe I’m getting back to normal, but even then it doesn’t feel like it’s fully gone. It’s more like it’s quieter for a while. Then it comes back up again, or I notice I’m still carrying it around. So… yeah, most of the day, most days, I’d say.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t really see things, not like visually, at least not that I can think of. But hearing, yeah, sometimes. It’s kind of hard to say out loud because it sounds… I don’t know, dramatic or something.

The main thing is I’ll hear the old headset beep from work, like the sound when a call comes in, even when my laptop is closed and I’m not logged in or anything. I’ll actually look over like I missed a call, and then there’s nothing. No phone ringing, no notification, nothing.

And sometimes it’s like a supervisor-type voice saying my name, or saying “too slow.” Not a whole conversation, more like a quick phrase. But it feels real enough in the moment that I react to it. Then I check and realize nobody’s there, or my computer’s shut, and I feel stupid and kind of shaken up.
Have there been times when you felt unusually up, energized, or irritable when those voices were happening?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think of it as “up,” exactly. Like, I wouldn’t say I’m suddenly in a great mood or energized in a good way when it happens.

If anything, I get kind of on edge or embarrassed afterward, because I’ll react like it was real and then realize there wasn’t anything there. But I haven’t really tracked whether it lines up with me being unusually irritable or wired. Sometimes I’m already tense, I guess, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean.
Have you ever heard those voices during a time when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think so. That’s part of what makes it confusing for me, honestly, because it’s not only when I’m really low.

There have been stretches, maybe a few weeks at a time, where my mood was more… I don’t want to say great, but closer to normal. Like I was getting up, getting things done, answering messages, doing basic stuff without it feeling impossible. And during those times, I still sometimes heard that supervisor-type voice, or I’d get really sure that the old ticketing software was flagging me or alerting me somehow, even when I wasn’t actually in it.

So yeah, it has happened when I wasn’t feeling especially depressed. I might still be stressed or kind of watchful, but not in that heavy depressed place. That’s why it freaks me out a little, because I can’t just explain it as “oh, I was having a bad mood day.”
Was there ever a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing those voices even though you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think there has been. I don’t have it marked on a calendar or anything, so I’m a little nervous saying it like it’s exact, but yes, there have been stretches that were more than just a day or two.

Like, a few weeks where I wasn’t in that really depressed place. My mood was more normal — not amazing, but I could get up, do chores, answer messages, handle basic things without everything feeling impossible. And even during those stretches, I still heard the supervisor-type voice sometimes, like saying my name or making some comment, or I’d get this really strong feeling that the old ticketing software was flagging me or alerting me even though I wasn’t actually using it.

So… yes, I’d say there were at least a couple weeks where that was happening and I wasn’t feeling depressed in the way I usually mean it. That’s one of the parts that bothers me, because it makes it harder to explain away as just my mood being bad.
Across the whole time since these problems started, have you been depressed for most of that time?

Yeah… I think, if I’m being honest, probably yes. Not every single day at the same intensity, but most of the time since all this started there’s been this kind of depressed layer underneath everything.

Some weeks are lighter, like I can function more normally and I’m not crying or completely shut down or anything. But even then, the sadness is usually still kind of there in the background, and the guilt too — like this constant feeling that I’ve messed things up or I should be doing better than I am. And I don’t get interested in things the way I used to. Even when I’m having a “better” week, it’s more like I’m managing, not like I feel genuinely okay.

Sleep has been part of that too. It shifts around, but it’s been a pretty regular problem through most of this. So I wouldn’t say I’ve been severely depressed every moment, but overall, yeah, most of the time since it started, those depressed feelings and the low interest and guilt and sleep stuff have been hanging around.
Have you ever had a period where you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re saying it, like needing way less sleep but still feeling energized.

My sleep has definitely been off at different times, but when I don’t sleep much, I usually feel it. I’m tired, foggy, kind of worn down. I don’t remember having a stretch where I was only sleeping a few hours and then waking up feeling great or charged up or like I didn’t need rest.

There might have been nights where I stayed up too late or couldn’t settle down, but that felt more like bad sleep than extra energy, if that makes sense. So… no, I don’t think I’ve had that kind of period.
During those weeks when you weren’t depressed, were the voices still there?

Yeah, they were still there. Not constantly every minute, but yes.

Those were the weeks that kind of confused me the most, honestly, because my mood was closer to normal — like I was getting up, doing chores, answering messages, keeping up with basic stuff — and I wasn’t feeling that heavy depressed feeling as much. But even then, I’d still hear that supervisor-type voice sometimes, or I’d get this very strong feeling that the old ticketing software was flagging me or sending some kind of alert about me, even though I wasn’t actually using it.

So… yeah, during those better mood stretches, it didn’t fully go away. That’s why I don’t feel like I can say it only happens when I’m depressed.
